title: One-Step Counter Program Simulation
statement: Let $P$ be a counter program with $R$ registers and labels in a set $\Lambda$. Fix a starting label $l_0\in\Lambda$, a Boolean $lm$, natural numbers $n,p,B$, a bit string $u$, and an oracle $o$ with two indices. Suppose that for every $h\in\mathbb N$, the oracle answers whether $h<|u|$ at index $0$ and returns the bit of $u$ at position $h$ (or $0$ if that position is beyond the end) at index $1$, when queried on the encoding of $(1^n,\mathrm{bits}(h))$. Let $l\in\Lambda$, let $\rho$ assign a natural number to each of the $R$ registers, and let $ps,tm\in\mathbb N$ and $out$ be a bit string, with $|out|\le p$, every value of $\rho$ at most $B$, and $ps,|out|,tm\le B$. Let $s'$ be the one-step successor of the state with label $l$, registers $\rho$, input position $ps$, and output $out$, on input $u$; suppose every register value and the input position and output length in $s'$ are at most $B$. Then either $s'$ is halted with output $out$, and the associated simulation halts with answer false, or $s'$ has a label $l'$. In the latter case, if $|s'.out|\le p$, the simulation reaches the configuration for $s'$ at label $l'$ with some time-register value at most $B$; if $|s'.out|>p$, it halts with answer $\mathbf{1}_{p<|s'.out|}$ when $lm$ is true, and otherwise with the bit of $s'.out$ at position $p$, taking that bit to be $0$ if absent. In both cases, every earlier simulation configuration satisfies the following invariant: each counter is at most $B$, every equality test between two registers compares distinct registers, input-word comparisons are made only on valid encodings of the required form, and each oracle call uses distinct argument registers.
